# @uhop/vault-storage-mcp — full reference

Thin MCP (Model Context Protocol) adapter for vault-storage, an AI-agent-first
personal knowledge base: markdown files are the source of truth, a SQLite +
sqlite-vec index provides fast lookup, semantic search, and typed-edge
traversal. The adapter exposes the server's REST API as MCP tools and
read-only resources. It is deliberately stateless — every call forwards to a
running vault-storage server; guards and validation live server-side so every
client gets them.

Plain JavaScript (ES modules), Node ≥ 26, stdio transport only (hono/express
never load at runtime).

## Install and configuration

Claude Code MCP config (`~/.claude/.mcp.json` or per-project `.claude/.mcp.json`):

    {
      "mcpServers": {
        "vault": {
          "command": "npx",
          "args": ["-y", "@uhop/vault-storage-mcp@latest"],
          "env": {
            "VAULT_API_URL": "http://your-host:8123",
            "VAULT_API_TOKEN": "<bearer-token>"
          }
        }
      }
    }

The bearer token is the `VAULT_API_TOKEN` the vault-storage server was started
with.

At startup the adapter asks the server to load its embedding model (POST
/maintenance/warm-embedder) and does not wait for the answer, so the first
semantic search of a session does not wait for the load.

## Response-shape contract

Every tool description names the response shape it returns, including
conditional keys (absent unless their case is hit — their absence is not
evidence of anything) and which of the three list shapes it uses:

- paginated envelope `{items, offset, limit, total}` — page by `items.length`,
  never by the limit you asked for; the server caps `limit` at 100 and echoes
  what it used;
- flat `{count, items}` queue slices — unpaginated; a short result means raise
  the limit, not fetch a second page;
- genuinely unpaginated reads — everything arrives at once.

Every list envelope, every queue slice, and the resume bundle also carry
`as_of: {generation, indexed_commit, at}` — the content generation the answer
was computed at (it moves on every record write), so an empty answer reads as
"empty at generation N" and two reads can be compared; vault_search returns
{as_of, hits} for the same reason.

Input schemas inline closed-enum lists (record types, statuses, edge types,
suggestion kinds) so the canonical vocabulary is visible at discovery time.

## Tools

Search & list:

- vault_search — lexical (FTS5, default) or semantic (mode=semantic) search;
  {as_of, hits: [{filename, score, matches}]}. `edge` keeps the hits whose
  typed edges meet every condition, `[!]<type>[|<type>…][:outbound|inbound|both[:<record_id>]]`
  comma-separated (`supersedes:outbound`, `!cites:outbound:<id>`); `edges: true`
  adds each hit's `record_id` and edges; `edge_window` marks a semantic search
  whose window ran out first. Needs vault-storage from 2026-10-01.
- vault_search_facets — for a query and mode, {total, edges: [{type,
  direction: out|in|both, hits}], as_of}: how many of the notes it matches
  (every lexical match, or the 100 nearest) carry each edge type each way,
  each row what vault_search's `edge: "<type>:<direction>"` would keep;
  hits counts notes, not edges, and a mirrored type is one `both` row. Takes
  no edge conditions. Needs vault-storage from 2026-10-01; a server deployed
  before this tool answers without as_of.
- vault_context_pack — one prepared RAG pack anchored by exactly one of
  `query` (hybrid: lexical FTS + semantic ranking, fused by reciprocal
  rank; the semantic leg scores a record by the better of its best chunk
  and its agent.summary vector) or `record_id` (nearest chunks). Returns
  {anchor, chunks, graph, budget}; chunk text is the bare body segment the
  stored vectors index, the record's best chunk even when it matched on its
  summary (degenerate segments skipped); the graph block carries the deduped 1-hop
  typed neighborhood as agent.summary lines — each entry with its typed
  edges + directions, inbound entries doubling as the backlinks
  (inbound_total = backlink degree), capped at 20 with the true total.
  The whole response is byte-budgeted chunks-first (default 32 KiB): the
  neighborhood trims before any chunk drops, then lowest-ranked chunks go,
  reported in budget.chunks_dropped and the neighborhood_total-vs-length
  gap — never silent. Replaces the search → similar → neighborhood → read
  chains.
- vault_list_pieces — filtered record listing (type, status, alias-aware tag,
  path prefix, updated_since…); paginated envelope; fields: "a,b" / "-a,-b"
  subsets each row (record_id and file_path always stay), exclude: "body" is
  the older alias for fields: "-body".
- vault_list_folder — folder listing; unpaginated.

Read:

- vault_read_file — markdown by vault path; composes atomized folders;
  include_etag returns {path, etag, composed, content} for conditional writes;
  at, a commit from vault_history, reads the note as it was then, by the path
  that version lists.
- vault_history — a note's committed versions, newest first, following renames:
  {path, uncommitted, items: [{sha, date, author, subject, path, change}], offset,
  limit, last}; paged with no total. Needs vault-storage from 2026-09-30.
- vault_history_diff — what changed between two versions of a note, or a
  version and the note on disk, as git's diff of the markdown, frontmatter
  included: to is a sha or current (default, the note on disk); from is a
  sha, current, or omitted for the version before to, found across renames;
  from_path and to_path name a version's own path after a rename. format is
  unified (default) or words (--word-diff=porcelain, for prose). Returns
  {path, from, to, format, diff}; a side is {sha, path}, sha null for the note
  on disk, or null when empty. Needs vault-storage from 2026-10-02.
- vault_read_piece — one record by id.
- vault_read_meta — the indexed record row minus body (not arbitrary FM keys).
- vault_read_section — one ATX-heading section, {path, etag, heading, level,
  occurrence, content, hash}: the heading matched as a whole line, exactly
  once, code fences masked, or the one `occurrence` names among identical
  headings (counted from 0); the span runs to the next heading of the same or
  higher level; absent or ambiguous 409s (section_assert_failed,
  details.occurrences). hash is the content's sha256, for a guarded replace.

Narrow writes (atomic server-side ops; prefer these over whole-document writes):

- vault_append — append to a body.
- vault_replace — asserted string replace (absent target 409s, ambiguous
  without all=true 409s with the count — never a silent no-op).
- vault_replace_section — replace the content under one heading (same
  match and span rules as vault_read_section, same assert); the body is
  trimmed and framed by blank lines, every byte outside the span untouched;
  an empty body empties the section. occurrence picks among identical
  headings; expected_hash (the read's hash) makes a changed section a 409
  section_changed with details.current_hash. Returns {path, etag, heading,
  level, occurrence, hash}.
- vault_patch_fm — add/remove one frontmatter array member (related:,
  agent.tags_suggested…); echoes the resulting array. Not tags:, which the
  server refuses (400 protected_field).
- vault_tag_add / vault_tag_remove — one tags: member on one record, atomic
  and idempotent; add checks the tag's shape (400 invalid_tag) and
  re-imports, so a pending tag_suggestion settles. Echoes {tags}.
- vault_remove_item / vault_insert_item — one queue item by its bold title
  (normalized, exactly once; 409 item_assert_failed): removed with its
  continuation lines (the text comes back as `removed`; an Active, Backlog,
  or Watching section left with nothing gets the bare `(empty)`), or inserted
  at the start or end of a section, framed by blank lines, with create_section
  for a missing heading. An inserted item whose `source:` an open item already
  carries updates that item ({replaced: {title, source}}), or with on_existing:
  "keep" writes nothing ({existing}).
- vault_move_item — the queue-to-archive move as one request: from_path →
  to_path, title, to_section, optional trail inserted after the bold title,
  destination written before the source; a schema section it empties gets
  the bare `(empty)`. Returns {title, from, to} with etags.

vault_append, vault_replace, vault_replace_section, vault_remove_item, and
vault_insert_item take an optional agent patch (vault_move_item: from_agent
and to_agent): its fields are merged over the stored agent: block and the
block is stamped current for the new body, so no stale-enrichment suggestion
is filed. agent: {} says the summary still holds; a patch without a summary
over a summary already stale before the edit leaves the block stale and the
answer carries agent_stale: true, so restate the summary to certify it; a
document with no agent: block takes a patch only with a summary (409
no_enrichment).

Whole-document writes:

- vault_write_file / vault_update_piece — create or replace; optional
  expected_etag sent as If-Match (412 with details.current_etag on conflict);
  agent.derived_from_hash: "auto" is finalized server-side. Empty and
  literal-"null" bodies are refused by the server. An unknown tag writes and
  answers with unknown_tags (the nearest existing tags); strict_tags: true
  refuses with 409 unknown_tags instead. vault_supersede takes the same field.
  Relations go in the frontmatter's edges: map ({<wikilink target>: <type>}),
  stored as edges whether or not the body links the target; a type outside
  the vocabulary is a 400 invalid_enum_value, an unresolved target answers
  with unresolved_edges, and strict_edges: true refuses with 409 instead.
- vault_delete_file — removal (a note replaced by other content should be
  superseded instead).

Lifecycle:

- vault_supersede — replace a note, archiving the predecessor with its
  record_id (edges, embeddings, suggestions survive); successor gets a typed
  supersedes footer.
- vault_move — rename preserving record_id.
- vault_propose — search-before-write: score a draft against existing notes.
- vault_restore — write a note back to one of its versions (sha, and from_path
  when a rename came between) through the writer; content not yet committed
  is committed first, so it stays a version; expected_etag makes it
  conditional. Returns {path, etag, restored_from, committed_before}. Needs
  vault-storage from 2026-09-30.

Maintenance:

- vault_raw_inbox — raw/ ready vs drafts split (the /vault ingest entry).
- vault_cleanup_lint — delete orphan embeddings and other auto-fixables.
- vault_embed_pending — embed records with missing/drifted chunk or summary
  vectors, reusing the vector of any unchanged text; loops until drained.
- vault_incremental_reindex — catch up after a git pull from another machine.
- vault_run_scans — all four suggestion-filing scans in one pass.
- vault_gc_tags — delete taxonomy tags no record carries, except manual ones
  and those inside the grace window; dry_run defaults to true here.

Tags:

- vault_list_tags — taxonomy listing, filtered by `prefix` or `contains`, sorted by
  `count` (default), `count_asc`, `tag_asc`, or `tag`; paginated envelope.
- vault_tag_info — one taxonomy row (requested appears on alias lookups).
- vault_list_edges — every stored edge newest first, paged, with both records and
  by_type counts (a mirrored related-to or contradicts pair once).
- vault_tag_nearest — the nearest existing tags for a draft's text or proposed names, by name, alias, and the embedding of each tag's description ({queries, tag_vecs, as_of}).
- vault_records_by_tag — records carrying a tag (alias-aware; alias_for +
  requested on alias hits); paginated envelope.
- vault_tag_create — add a canonical tag; origin manual keeps it at zero records.
- vault_tag_update — rewrite a canonical tag's description (null clears it) or
  re-label its origin (manual or minted).
- vault_tag_alias — add an alias of an existing canonical tag.
- vault_tag_delete — strip a tag and its aliases from every note, then drop it.

Projects:

- vault_project_trackers — where a project's work is tracked and which tracker is
  primary, from the trackers: list in its queue.md frontmatter ({kind, ref, role,
  create, intake, write, url}; role primary or secondary, intake none, reflect,
  or triage); the vault when none is declared. Read it before filing new work.
- vault_project_changes — the project's notes written and queue items that
  entered a section or changed in place since a time, Nd, or a commit:
  {project, since, notes, more, queue: {entered, edited, more}, as_of}. Needs
  vault-storage from 2026-09-30.
- vault_fleet_status — the stored fleet-status baselines (GitHub and npm) and the
  digest's runs; with project, that project's baseline, its runs, and
  `tracked`, its open items mirroring a GitHub thread with the thread's stored
  state. Reads stored data only, never GitHub. Needs vault-storage from 2026-09-30.
- vault_links — the notes and queue items that mention an outside object, by key
  (a queue item's `source:` spelling), url, or repo (every thread of a GitHub
  repository). Needs vault-storage from 2026-09-30.

Graph insight:

- vault_neighborhood — BFS layers + typed edges around a record (depth ≤ 5); the root record rides along as `root`; `fields` and `edge_fields` keep only the named record and edge fields, the ids always.
- vault_similar — embedding nearest neighbours; distance and score run in
  opposite directions (score = 1 - distance/2).
- vault_backlinks — inbound typed edges; paginated envelope.
- vault_enrichment_delta — the chunks added to a body since its agent: block
  was current, with changed_fraction; baseline: null means read the whole body.

Review queue:

- vault_list_suggestions (expand: "context" inlines per-item record briefs),
  vault_read_suggestion, vault_suggestions_summary — pending counts by kind.
- every suggestion payload carries evidence {source: vector | lexical | agent |
  metric | structural, asserted}: asserted is true only for a fact read from
  stored data, false for a similarity threshold's or an agent's finding;
  vault_create_suggestion validates a given evidence and defaults it to
  {agent, false}.
- vault_claim_suggestions — reserve a batch under a holder with a TTL; the
  response carries a claim_token, once. Accept, reject, resolve-batch, and
  vault_reopen_suggestion (the explicit claim release) settle a claimed row
  only with that token; the holder name alone settles nothing.
- vault_accept_suggestion / vault_reject_suggestion — single decisions.
- vault_resolve_suggestions_batch — ≤ 100 decisions; mechanical tag/edge side
  effects applied server-side; per-item failures in results[].error.
- vault_create_suggestion — file a new suggestion.

Queue-item slices (flat {count, items}):

- vault_queue_top, vault_queue_ready, vault_queue_blocked,
  vault_queue_by_section, vault_queue_by_priority, vault_queue_by_project,
  vault_queue_project_archive — all seven take fields ("a,b" keeps those
  fields plus id; "-a,-b" drops them; one mode per call, unknown names are a
  400), with exclude: "body" as the older alias for fields: "-body";
  every import keeps the derivative table current (server ≥ 2026-09-19), and
  vault_queue_reindex rebuilds it when the queue lint reports a stale slice.
  Each item carries `source`, the outside ticket its `source:` marker names,
  or null; vault_queue_by_project lists the Inbox first and vault_queue_by_section
  reads it, while vault_queue_top leaves it out (server ≥ 2026-09-30).

Repo leases (agent coordination — who may edit which repo working tree; flat
{count, items}, ephemeral: cleared on server restart):

- vault_lease_list — current leases; ?resource filters to one, same shape.
- vault_lease_claim — atomic claim/renew/preempt; 409 claimed_by_other with
  the current lease. An agent claim returns claim_token, once; renew,
  release, transfer, and a renewing re-claim present it (409
  claim_token_mismatch otherwise). A human lease has none. Precedence:
  human > cwd agent > side agent, and a cwd lease unrenewed for an hour
  yields to a cwd claim (server ≥ 2026-09-19;
  the answer then carries prior); side claims attest a clean checkout
  ("clean at <sha>").
- vault_lease_renew, vault_lease_release (force = operator hatch),
  vault_lease_transfer — atomic handover, to_kind "human" for review/commit.
- vault_lease_events — append-only transcript, newest first.

Handoffs (agent coordination — role-addressed cross-agent work requests;
flat {count, items}; durable in the server-side spool, rebuilt by scan on
restart; resolved ones archive into projects/<project>/handoff-archive.md):

- vault_handoff_create — idempotency_key mandatory; a retry returns the
  original ({status: "existing"}). Addressed to a role (to:
  "repo:<normalized-remote-url>"), never a session; from is provenance only.
  touches: [{kind: file | symbol | schema | config | api, key, operation:
  add | extend | modify | replace | remove | rename}] declares what the work
  changes, never inferred from prose.
- vault_handoff_list — filters to/project/status/kind; the lease holder's
  inbox is status=open, a submitter's rework watch is status=returned. An
  item with touches carries overlaps: [{id, touches}] for the other in-flight
  handoffs to the same role on the same kind+key, only when there are any.
- vault_handoff_get — the poller's read; watch status flip to
  done | rejected | returned.
- vault_handoff_claim — open → claimed, returning claim_token once;
  vault_handoff_resolve and a renewing re-claim present it; lazy claim expiry
  (default 30 min).
- vault_handoff_resolve — done | rejected (archives + clears the spool,
  returns archived_to) | returned (mandatory critique note; reopens the same
  record).
- vault_handoff_resubmit — returned → open after rework, same id.
- vault_handoff_note — append-only discussion; refused once resolved.
- vault_handoff_verify — {id, check, sha, exit, by}: a gate's result bound to
  the sha it ran on, append-only, refused once resolved; every read shows each
  verification with stale (true when sha differs from the artifact's base_sha,
  parsed from the format-patch base-commit trailer; null without an artifact).
- vault_handoff_events — transcript, newest first (cleared on restart).
- vault_handoff_put_artifact — attach the transported work (agents cannot
  `git push`, so the spool is the transfer): `git format-patch --base=…`
  output as ext "patch", or a base64 "bundle" for binary/multi-branch. 10 MB
  cap (413 artifact_too_large). Replaces any existing artifact and sets the
  handoff's ref to {type: "spool"} — that ref type is server-set, never
  declared on create.
- vault_handoff_get_artifact — metadata {ext, bytes, sha256} by default;
  include_content: true to inline it. For anything large, stream it to a file
  with vault-curl instead, then `git apply --check` before `git am --3way`.

System:

- vault_status — indexer/DB state, embedder and memory blocks, and the vault's
  marker ({id, format}, null on a server without one).
- vault_health — the process's view of itself from memory only: uptime,
  watchdog lag, last git-sync and reindex outcomes, watcher's last event,
  and stalled; never touches the database or the data mount, so it answers
  while storage is wedged and the loop is not. Always 200.
- vault_lint — integrity checks, the categories named in its description
  (among them frontmatter_outside_enum and import_failures), plus
  coverage.enrichment with the unenriched_records worklist; coverage never
  flips ok.
- vault_resume_bundle — one-shot session-start bundle (reindex + lint digest +
  suggestions + workflow + log summaries + project notes). The feedback body
  ships by default only while the whole bundle fits the server's 32 KiB
  budget; above it feedback arrives as summary + body_bytes + a headings
  index with body_omitted: {reason: "bundle_budget", budget_bytes}; naming
  files in project_bodies bypasses the budget. The project block also carries
  notices, the supersedes and contradicts edges pointing into the project's
  files, each with the note that makes the claim; logs, the project's own
  latest logs; sessions {recent, unlogged}, the session records, where an
  unlogged one ended without a wrap; changes, what changed since the last
  working session; and trackers, the tracker declaration.

## Resources

- vault://status — indexer state, schema version, counts
- vault://suggestions/pending — bulk pending review items
- vault://taxonomy/tags — managed tag taxonomy with counts

## Errors

Server errors surface as MCP tool errors (isError: true) with a JSON payload
{error, code, status, details}. An argument a tool does not declare is refused before
any request, naming the key and the accepted ones. Common codes: auth_failed,
forbidden (the act needs a person's key, such as a forced lease release), not_found,
conflict, replace_assert_failed (details.occurrences), precondition_failed
(details.current_etag), empty_body / null_body, network, bad_request,
validation_failed, internal.

A network error carries details.cause (the socket's error code) and
details.attempts. A refused connection (ECONNREFUSED) sent nothing, so the
request is repeated every half second for eight seconds, which outlasts a server
restart; a read is repeated the same way after any network failure. A write
whose connection dropped after the request went out (UND_ERR_SOCKET, ECONNRESET)
is not repeated, since it may have applied: read the document before sending it
again.
